newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey considers strike on Cyprus missiles - agency.
newsitem.headline: Turkey considers strike on Cyprus missiles - agency.

text.p: Turkey's state-run news agency said on Thursday that Ankara was considering a military strike in the future to knock out missile launchers due to be deployed in Cyprus.
"Ankara is seriously considering an operation against the missile launchers when the time comes if Turkey's warnings to the Greek Cypriot administration are not heeded," the Anatolian agency said.

It quoted a high-ranking official as saying that Turkey could carry out military exercises and forge closer ties with the Turkish Cypriot community to pressure Greek Cypriots to drop a plan to deploy Russian anti-aircraft missiles on the island.
"These measures will become clear very shortly," the unnamed official said.

Turkey has accused the Cypriot government of trying to change the balance of forces on Cyprus with a deal announced last weekend to buy Russian S-300 surface-to-air missiles that could neutralise Turkish air superiority on the divided island.
Earlier, Defence Minister Turhan Tayan said that Turkey would use all possible means to halt the missile deployment. It is unclear when the missiles will be delivered.
